name: Chronicle Labs

modes.label: Native service
modes.note: Not a rentable compute sandbox. Chronicle Labs is an agent testing/backtesting platform: it builds simulated 'worlds' of service twins (simulated vendor APIs such as Slack/Linear/Salesforce seeded from production data) and runs the customer's agent (their own run command) against task suites inside Chronicle's evaluation sandbox, scoring the results. Trials run in per-trial smolvm (libkrun) microVMs on KVM; the orchestrator also has Daytona and Docker drivers. No public price, no CPU/RAM tariff; sales/demo-led with a free signup.

caveats: Demo-led agent testing/backtesting platform (YC Spring 2026, Active); /pricing returns 404 and no rates are published anywhere (site, llms.txt, docs). It does not rent arbitrary compute: customers run their own agent command inside Chronicle's evaluation sandbox against service twins (simulated vendor APIs). Entry points: free signup and a 'Free Agent Audit'.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

Documented limits: evaluation concurrency 1-32 trials (default 4); 8 agents and 200 trials per run; twins live 1-720 h (default 72, ttl_hours) and count against an org 'twin capacity' (403 when exceeded); 429 = 'Over the concurrency or trial limit'; 403 'Your organization doesn't have sandbox access' (sandbox access is gated per org). Capacity sizes per plan are not published.
Free entry points exist (free signup at app.chronicle-labs.com, free agent audit), but no free-tier size, credit amount or paid tariff is published; free.* stay null.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Save a running machine mid-execution, rewind it, or branch it into copies that keep running from the same point. Checkpoints capture RAM, CPU state and disks; branches are copy-on-write children of a live machine.
snapshot_on_demand.note: smolvm (the microVM Chronicle runs trials in): memory INCLUDED (RAM+CPU+disk); new machines boot from a checkpoint (`machine create --from agent.checkpoint`) and live COW branches. Chronicle's blog: bake a world, publish .smolmachine artifact via OCI, rehydrate/fork many times.

egress_allowlist.quote: smolvm adds a second, independent layer at the VM boundary: networking is disabled by default, and enabling it requires an explicit domain allowlist.
egress_allowlist.note: Enforced outside the guest at the VM boundary. Chronicle policies: deny_all / mocked_only / passthrough_record (vendor domains). smolvm allows --allow-host / --allow-host-pattern (domains, wildcards) AND --allow-cidr (IP/CIDR), so level=both.

ingress_rules.quote: Networking is disabled by default. Enabling --net, port forwarding, or host services expands the workload's reachable surface.
ingress_rules.note: Ports closed by default; you explicitly publish port mappings (Smolfile `ports = ["8000:8000"]`, max 64 mappings) and there is an [auth] table. You choose which ports are exposed. Chronicle trials typically run with no inbound network.

guest_firewall.note: smolvm gives each workload a hardware-isolated libkrun microVM with its own guest kernel and (untrusted) root; a full guest kernel means iptables/nftables inside the VM take effect. Derived.

secret_proxy.quote: The guest receives an opaque placeholder in the environment variable it expects; the host replaces the placeholder with the real value only on HTTPS requests to the hosts you allow, and only inside a request header. The value never enters the machine, its record, or a checkpoint.
secret_proxy.note: Real secret proxy in the smolvm substrate: register credentials for ARBITRARY HTTPS hosts (e.g. api.notion.com, api.github.com) => any-http. HTTPS + request-header only; non-HTTP protocols (DB/SSH/git) and query-string/body use NOT covered (refused or literal placeholder). Chronicle's own trials mainly mock vendor APIs (worldd), so real creds are rarely used; capability belongs to the sandbox tech.

volume_shared.quote: Isolated: one run must never see another workspace's data or mutate another trial's state.
volume_shared.note: Strict per-VM isolation by design; branches are copy-on-write children, not a shared read-write filesystem mounted by several running machines. No shared/network volume documented.

isolation.quote: Each workload runs in a hardware-virtualized VM with its own guest kernel on Hypervisor.framework (macOS), KVM (Linux)... libkrun is the VMM
isolation.note: Trials run in per-trial smolvm microVMs (libkrun VMM on KVM/Linux), a full hardware-isolated VM with its own guest kernel - closest taxonomy bucket is full VM on KVM, though the actual VMM is libkrun (a lightweight microVM library), not literally QEMU.

image_oci.quote: Images use the OCI format, so anything on Docker Hub, ghcr.io or another registry boots as a microVM, with no Docker daemon.
image_oci.note: Chronicle's own worlds are also published/pulled as OCI artifacts (.smolmachine via OCI registry per the engineering blog).

docker_inside.quote: Runs Docker Engine in a bare Alpine VM. Init commands run directly in the VM as root via VmExec, so Docker gets full kernel privileges without any capability restrictions.
docker_inside.note: Documented example runs dockerd (and even k3d/k3s) inside the smolvm guest kernel that Chronicle's trials use.

desktop.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform that turns production data into staging environments...runs agents against replicated production environments
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. A generic Wayland/VNC desktop example exists in the underlying open-source smolvm substrate, but Chronicle's own testing/backtesting product exposes no GUI/desktop to customers.

browser.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform...runs agents against replicated production environments derived from real traffic
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Chronicle mocks vendor APIs (worldd) rather than driving a real browser; a headless-browser example exists in the smolvm substrate but is not a Chronicle product feature.

computer_use.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform...runs agents against replicated production environments
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no screenshot/click desktop-driving API found.

anti_bot.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform that turns production data into staging environments
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - this is an internal agent evaluation platform, not a web-scraping/bot-evasion product.

captcha_solving.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform that turns production data into staging environments
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

ssh.quote: runs agents against replicated production environments derived from real traffic
ssh.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - trials are ephemeral, orchestrator-driven sandboxes (created/destroyed per trial) rather than machines customers interactively SSH into.

snapshot.quote: Save a running machine mid-execution, rewind it, or branch it into copies that keep running from the same point. Checkpoints capture RAM, CPU state and disks
snapshot.note: smolvm checkpoints capture RAM + CPU state + disk (full memory snapshot), matching Chronicle's card feature_evidence for snapshot_on_demand.

snapshot_auto.quote: smolvm machine checkpoint --name agent -o agent.checkpoint        # save it, processes and all
snapshot_auto.note: Checkpointing requires an explicit CLI/API call; no documented automatic save-on-stop/idle/timeout behavior.

fork.quote: smolvm machine branch --from agent --name try-1                   # live copy-on-write child
fork.note: Branching (forking) a machine into new copy-on-write copies is a core documented feature.

fork_running.quote:
smolvm machine start --name agent --branchable
smolvm machine branch --from agent --name try-1                   # live copy-on-write child
fork_running.note: Branch is taken from a running (--branchable) machine without stopping it.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Save a running machine mid-execution, rewind it, or branch it into copies that keep running from the same point.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Live branches are copy-on-write clones of a running machine, so they include memory/process state (clones keep running from the same point).

pause_resume.quote: stop without losing execution with [pause and resume](docs/pause-resume.md)

wake_on_request.quote: A trial begins when the orchestrator selects the next case from the pinned Dataset Version and asks the sandbox driver for an environment.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - trials are explicitly created by the orchestrator per test case, not woken automatically by an inbound network request.

persistent_disk.quote: Machines persist across restarts, and any OCI image works, including ones you build locally.

volume_attach.quote: Declare a machine in a Smolfile: image, resources, ports, mounts and network policy in one checked-in file.
volume_attach.note: Smolfile 'mounts' plus -v host-dir mount flags document attachable volumes/directories.

auto_stop_idle.quote: When the trial finishes, the machine is destroyed.
auto_stop_idle.note: derived: trial VMs are ephemeral by design and are torn down automatically once the run ends, functioning like an auto-stop rather than a persistent always-on VM.

live_resize.quote: Defaults: 4 vCPUs, 8 GiB RAM. Memory is elastic via virtio balloon and idle vCPUs sleep in the hypervisor... Override with --cpus and --mem.
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM are set at machine-creation time (--cpus/--mem); memory ballooning is automatic elasticity, not a customer-triggered live resize API for a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: runs agents against replicated production environments derived from real traffic
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - customers bring their own agent/run command; no preinstalled coding-agent harness templates (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) documented.

harness_api.quote: runs agents against replicated production environments derived from real traffic
harness_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no first-party API to drive a preinstalled coding harness.

own_agent_api.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Chronicle evaluates the customer's own agent; it does not offer its own browser/computer-use/research task agent.

mcp_server.quote: docs, chronicle-typescript, chronicle-python, chronicle-go, chronicle-java, chronicle-dotnet, chronicle-rust, studio-desktop
mcp_server.note: No MCP-server repo/package found in Chronicle Labs' public GitHub org or docs as of check date.

lang_python.quote: pip install chroniclelabs ... The ChronicleLabs Python library provides convenient access to the ChronicleLabs APIs from Python.
lang_python.note: First-party Python SDK (chroniclelabs on PyPI, chronicle-labs-ai/chronicle-python on GitHub) for the Chronicle API.

lang_node.quote: npm i -s @chroniclelabs/api-client ... The ChronicleLabs TypeScript library provides convenient access to the ChronicleLabs APIs from TypeScript.

public_ipv4.quote: networking is disabled by default, and enabling it requires an explicit domain allowlist.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - trial microVMs run with no network by default and no public-IP exposure documented.

inbound_https.quote: networking is disabled by default, and enabling it requires an explicit domain allowlist.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - no documented feature to reach a port on the trial VM via a public HTTPS URL; egress-only allowlisting is the documented network model.

egress_http_rules.quote: smolvm machine run --net --image alpine --allow-host-pattern registry.npmjs.org -- wget -qO- https://registry.npmjs.org   # exact host only
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is documented at the domain/hostname-pattern and CIDR level (--allow-host, --allow-host-pattern, --allow-cidr); no HTTP method/path-level rule granularity is documented.

gpu.quote: We are also watching smolvm's GPU path—Vulkan through virtio-gpu and CUDA API remoting—as a way to bring heavier scoring models inside the isolation boundary rather than running them beside it.
gpu.note: GPU support in the smolvm substrate is exploratory/roadmap per Chronicle's own blog, not a currently shipped Chronicle product feature.

windows.quote: Chronicle Labs integrates with 100+ production tools
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - trial guests are Linux-only microVMs (card already sets linux:true, others null); no Windows guest machines.

macos.quote: Each workload runs in a hardware-virtualized VM with its own guest kernel on Hypervisor.framework (macOS), KVM (Linux), or the Windows Hypervisor Platform (Windows)
macos.note: macOS/Windows are only supported as smolvm *hosts*; the guest is always Linux, so no macOS guest machines are offered.

arm64.quote: macOS Apple Silicon | arm64 Linux ... Linux aarch64 | aarch64 Linux | KVM (/dev/kvm)
arm64.note: The smolvm substrate supports arm64 Linux guests on both Apple Silicon and Linux aarch64 hosts.

self_host.quote: Chronicle Labs is an AI agent testing and validation platform that turns production data into staging environments
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope - Chronicle Labs itself is a hosted SaaS platform (sign up / book a demo); only the separate open-source smolvm substrate tool is self-hostable, not the Chronicle product.

open_source.quote: Chronicle Labs is a Y Combinator-backed company building infrastructure for teams running AI agents in production.
open_source.note: Chronicle Labs' own platform is closed-source SaaS. Its VM substrate, smolvm, is separately open source under Apache-2.0, but that is a different project (smol-machines), not the Chronicle Labs product.
